Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

produce verb

bring out, show

also bring out, take out, pull out

classical

Plaut. Am. 769: Vīn' prōferrī pateram? — Prōferrī volō.
Cic. Rosc. Com. 29: ex arcā (Lewis & Short)

prōferō, prōferre, prōtulī, prōlātum

verb, irregular

bring out, produce

Of bringing a thing out from where it was kept or hidden, to show it: a letter, a witness, money from a chest.

Examples

  • at ille prōfert ipsum porcellum ē sinū

    but he produces the piglet itself from under his cloakPhaedr. 5.5.37

  • flāvaque dē rubrō prōmere mella cadō

    and to bring out golden honey from the red jarMart. 1.55.10

  • Cito prōferte stolam prīmam, et induite illum

    Quick, bring out the best robe, and put it on himVulg. Lc. 15.22

Other words

  • prōmō, prōmere, prōmpsī, prōmptum — take out, bring out (from a store)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 829: prōmpsistī tū illī vīnum?; Mart. 1.55.10: flāvaque dē rubrō prōmere mella cadō

    Of wine from the jar, money from the treasury, books from the shelf.

See also show, produce.

SourcesLewis & Short: profero · Lewis & Short: promo
